summary: Declared objectives evaluate bad-event ratios and honest covered-time gauge budgets from replicated claims, with paired burn alerts and native objective owner bindings

replay.detail: The incremental evaluator rebuilds its in-memory observations from durable replicated claims on restart or declaration revision.

schema.detail: No client-v0 fields or persistence tables change in this evaluator fragment. Existing objective JSON fields carry met, burning, exhausted, no-data, not-eligible and no-qualifying-events.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Ratio events deduplicate by source subject and event timestamp, with deterministic claim-ID ties. Gauge readings hold only until their next reading or max-age; unknown duration never counts as healthy. Thirty-day remaining budget is unknown until minimum coverage and samples are met. Both long and short burn windows must qualify and cross their declared rate; a short-only spike is diagnostic. Gauge short windows expand to at least one source cadence, long windows to at least two: hourly sources use fast 2h+1h and slow 6h+1h for the standard 14.4x/6x policy. A qualifying pair may burn before thirty-day coverage is established, but exhaustion requires eligible horizon evidence. Fleet native bindings inherit the source objective row and attach the declaration owner through the existing response pipeline.

manual.detail: Policies originate in objective declarations; no evaluator-specific manual step.

recovery.detail: Rollback restores the previous evaluator; source claims remain durable.
